title: Strict scalar-extension square for the specified quotient-cone augmentation
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism with $\ell$ invertible on both schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $W=X,Y$ put $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,W}$, $B_{F,W,m}=(\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^m)_W$ for $F=E,L$ and $m\geq1$, with quotient projections $\pi^F_{W,m}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $G_F=g^{-1}$ on completed-coefficient module complexes, transporting the action along the ring isomorphism $c_F:g^{-1}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}\simeq\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,X}$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. These maps satisfy $\pi^F_{X,m}c_F=c^g_{\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^m}g^{-1}(\pi^F_{Y,m})$. Tensor products below are sheaf tensor products and their total complexes [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

Let $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Put $Q=P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y$ and $Z=G_EP\otimes_{R_X}S_X$, with the chain isomorphism $b_P:Z\to G_LQ$, $g^{-1}p\otimes c_L(g^{-1}s_0)\mapsto g^{-1}(p\otimes s_0)$ [lem-weil-isomorphism-scalar-tensor-kflat-model]. For $F=E,L$ and $M=P,Q$, respectively, put
$$D_m^F(M)=\operatorname{Res}^F_m g_{F,m}^*(M\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}}B_{F,Y,m}),\qquad A_F(M)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_mD_m^F(M)\to\prod_mD_m^F(M))[-1],$$
where $g_{F,m}^*$ is finite-coefficient module pullback, $\operatorname{Res}^F_m$ restricts along $\pi^F_{X,m}$ and $s$ is induced by the actual quotient transitions [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Denote by $a^E_P:G_EP\to A_E(P)$ and $a^L_Q:G_LQ\to A_L(Q)$ the specified chain augmentations of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b): their shifted-product coordinate is zero and their $m$-th unshifted coordinate is $g^{-1}x\mapsto(g^{-1}(x\otimes1))\otimes1$.

Let $d_m:D_m^E(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X\to D_m^L(Q)$ and $\delta_P:A_E(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X\to A_L(Q)$ be exactly the same-index tower and whole-cone maps of [lem-weil-specified-pullback-comparison-alpha]. Thus on local tensors
$$d_m(((g^{-1}(p\otimes\bar a))\otimes b)\otimes s)=(g^{-1}(p\otimes\iota_m(\bar a)))\otimes(\iota_m(b)\pi^L_{X,m}(s)),$$
and $\delta_P$ applies $\prod_md_m$ to both cone coordinates, using the finite-free tensor/product identifications. Then there is an equality of actual chain maps of $S_X$-complexes
$$\delta_P\circ(a^E_P\otimes_{R_X}S_X)=a^L_Q\circ b_P:Z\longrightarrow A_L(Q).$$
Both sides have shifted-product coordinate zero; their common $m$-th unshifted coordinate on $y\otimes s$, for $y=g^{-1}p$ and $s=c_L(g^{-1}s_0)$, is
$$(g^{-1}(p\otimes1))\otimes\pi^L_{X,m}(s)\ \in g_{L,m}^*(Q\otimes_{S_Y}B_{L,Y,m}).$$
Here $Q\otimes_{S_Y}B_{L,Y,m}=P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{L,Y,m}$ uses $R_Y\to B_{L,Y,m}=(\iota_m)_Y\pi^E_{Y,m}$, and $p\otimes1$ in the displayed formula is in this latter complex. The equality concerns the entire cone with its fixed zero shifted coordinate, before localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Section 6.5, Lemma 6.5.9(4), pp. 50-51, for completed pullback; agent calculation from the specified quotient-tower comparisons. This coefficient-extension identity is not a quoted assertion of Bhatt–Scholze.

proof.text: Fix a degree $i$. By the section formula for inverse image along an isomorphism in [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image](1), sections of $G_EP^i$ can be written $y=g^{-1}p$ on the corresponding site object. The ring isomorphism $c_L$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] likewise writes a section of $S_X$ as $s=c_L(g^{-1}s_0)$. By the definition of sheaf tensor product as the sheafification of the sectionwise tensor product, it suffices to compare the two maps on these local pure tensors $y\otimes s$: sectionwise tensors are finite sums of pure tensors, and equality of their sheafified maps follows from the universal property of sheafification. Use these notations in the following calculations, for every $m\geq1$.

source.place: Section 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafified sectionwise tensor product; agent reduction using lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image(1).

proof.text: The shifted-product coordinate of $a^E_P$ is zero by its specified definition (b). After tensoring with $S_X$ this coordinate remains zero. The map $\delta_P$ of [lem-weil-specified-pullback-comparison-alpha] applies $\prod_m d_m$ separately to the two coordinates, so its shifted coordinate is still zero. The shifted coordinate of $a^L_Q\circ b_P$ is also zero, since $a^L_Q$ has zero shifted coordinate on every input. This compares the entire shifted-product component, not just its projections in the derived category.

source.place: Tag 08TC (definition-derived-limit), fixed cone representative specified in def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison(b); agent coordinate calculation.

proof.text: For the left composite, the $m$-th unshifted coordinate of $(a^E_P\otimes S_X)(y\otimes s)$ is $((g^{-1}(p\otimes1))\otimes1)\otimes s$. Substitute $\bar a=1$ and $b=1$ in the stated formula for $d_m$. Since $\iota_m$ preserves the unit, its image is exactly $$(g^{-1}(p\otimes1))\otimes\pi^L_{X,m}(s)\in D^L_m(Q).$$ Here the $p\otimes1$ on the output is in $P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{L,Y,m}$, identified with $Q\otimes_{S_Y}B_{L,Y,m}$ by the identification explicitly stated in [lem-weil-specified-pullback-comparison-alpha]. The canonical tensor/product map is the map whose $m$-th projection tensors the $m$-th projection, so this is the $m$-th coordinate of the actual left cone map.

source.place: Tag 03D6 (definition-pushforward), pullback tensor formula; Section 03EK (section-tensor-product); agent substitution in the specified d_m.

proof.text: For the right composite, the formula of [lem-weil-isomorphism-scalar-tensor-kflat-model] gives $b_P(y\otimes s)=g^{-1}(p\otimes s_0)$. The $m$-th unshifted coordinate after $a^L_Q$ is therefore $$(g^{-1}((p\otimes s_0)\otimes1))\otimes1.$$ In $Q\otimes_{S_Y}B_{L,Y,m}$ the tensor balancing relation sends $(p\otimes s_0)\otimes1$ to $p\otimes\pi^L_{Y,m}(s_0)$. Balancing in the finite module pullback then gives $$(g^{-1}(p\otimes1))\otimes c^g_{A_{L,m}}(g^{-1}(\pi^L_{Y,m}(s_0)))=(g^{-1}(p\otimes1))\otimes\pi^L_{X,m}(s).$$ The last equality is precisely $c^g_{A_{L,m}}g^{-1}(\pi^L_{Y,m})=\pi^L_{X,m}c_L$ from the structure-isomorphism clause of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Thus the right coordinate equals the left coordinate calculated above.

source.place: Tag 03D6 (definition-pushforward), module pullback; Section 03EK (section-tensor-product), balancing and associativity; agent calculation using the specified coefficient-square identity.

proof.text: The coordinate calculations hold for every local pure tensor in every degree, hence for all sections of $Z^i$ by additivity and sheafification as in Step 1. Maps into a product are determined by their component maps, and a map into the two-summand cone term is determined by both projections. Steps 2--4 therefore give equality of the degree-$i$ module maps into $A_L(Q)^i$ for every $i$. The maps in question are already chain maps by the stated constructions, and a morphism of complexes is its family of degree maps [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Consequently $\delta_P\circ(a^E_P\otimes_{R_X}S_X)=a^L_Q\circ b_P$ as actual chain maps, with the claimed common coordinates. No passage to localization is involved in this equality.

There is no dependency cycle and no SGA citation. Step 1: the section formula of lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image(1) gives y=g^{-1}p, and since c_L is an isomorphism s=c_L(g^{-1}s_0); the sheaf tensor is a sheafified presheaf tensor, so pure tensors suffice. Step 2: the shifted coordinate of a^E_P is 0 by def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison(b), and δ_P applies ∏d_m to both coordinates, so it stays 0 and matches the 0 of a^L_Q. Step 3: putting ā=b=1 into the d_m formula of the alpha node gives (g^{-1}(p⊗1))⊗π^L_{X,m}(s). Step 4: b_P(y⊗s)=g^{-1}(p⊗s_0). Under the alpha identification (p⊗s_0)⊗1 becomes p⊗π^L_{Y,m}(s_0), and moving that factor across the finite pullback tensor gives c^g g^{-1}π^L_{Y,m}(s_0)=π^L_{X,m}c_L(g^{-1}s_0)=π^L_{X,m}(s), which is the stated structure equation. This uses ρ_m=π^L restricted to R_Y, valid since ϖ_E^mO_E⊂ϖ_L^mO_L. Step 5: extensionality into products and cone summands, degree by degree. Edge cases checked: g=id with E=L, ramified e>1, m=1, the zero complex and the empty scheme. Bhatt–Scholze 6.5.9(4) on pp. 50-51 is about completed pullback and is correctly cited only as context, with proof_origin=agent. Not a duplicate: lem-weil-scalar-pullback-strict-cone-naturality only defines δ_P. The parent's step uses exactly this conclusion. No changes.
